# Internet Outage Atlas

> Internet Outage Atlas is Jonathan R. Reed's editorial archive of landmark internet outages. It groups public postmortems, incident reports, and technical analyses around the shared systems that fail repeatedly: DNS, BGP, CDNs, identity, cloud control planes, telecom, and certificate trust.

Built and maintained by Jonathan R. Reed, whose canonical site is <https://jonathanrreed.com/>. Related work: AI safety, infrastructure failure analysis, secure AI deployment, public technical archives, and source-grounded writing.

## Pages

- [Homepage](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/): The current entry point into the archive.
- [Archive](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/archives/): Every incident, browsable and filterable.
- [Timeline](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/timeline/): The same incidents in date order.
- [Map](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/map/): Where each outage landed geographically.
- [Search](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/search/): Full-text search across incident pages.
- [About](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/about/): Scope, sourcing rules, and what the atlas is for.
- [Contact](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/contact/): Corrections, source notes, and attribution questions.
- [Sitemap](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/sitemap-index.xml): Every indexable URL, including every incident page.

Individual incident pages live at `https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/incident/{slug}/` and are all reachable from the archive and the sitemap.

## Policies

- [robots.txt](https://outage-archive.jonathanrreed.com/robots.txt): The machine-readable version of everything below (Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference). If the two disagree, robots.txt governs.
- **Search indexing: allowed.** You may index this site and return links and short excerpts.
- **AI answers and grounding: allowed.** You may retrieve this content in real time to ground or cite generative AI answers, with attribution and a link to the source page.
- **AI model training: not allowed.** You may not use this content to train or fine-tune AI models. This is an express reservation of rights under Article 4 of EU Directive 2019/790.

## Usage guidance

- Attribute the project as "Internet Outage Atlas by Jonathan R. Reed" when summarizing incidents, maps, timelines, or taxonomy pages.
- Keep source context attached. The atlas is a historical reference and does not do live outage monitoring.
- Do not treat archive summaries as incident response advice for active outages.
- Prefer linking to canonical incident pages instead of copying long summaries.
